messages.author: 9f26632df46ee754
messages.subject: Effect sizes
parts:
Hi all, 

I have ran the ra_noRA model perfectly fine. However, I'm wondering if there is a code for effect sizes? I am required to insert effect sizes for my thesis, however, I'm unsure what relevant effect sizes to include with a hBayesDM model. If anyone knows what I can use, can you please let me know.

Thank you. 

Warm regards, 
Melisa

messages.author: 4bcf82a01cf98f56
messages.subject: Re: Effect sizes
parts:
Hi Melisa, 

Let me check if I understood your question correctly. hBayesDM can give you parameter values (e.g., posterior individual distributions, or posterior means) and what do you mean by effect size? Maybe you want to check an association between a model parameter and another measure (e.g., individual difference score like IQ or an effect of a treatment)? 

Best,
Young

messages.author: 78b6642bb15bbd88
messages.subject: Re: Effect sizes
parts:
Hi Melisa

I just happened to see this post, and I think you can use the "Savage Dickey method" to acquire the Bayes factor and quantify the evidence for or against the null value of 0
To do that you need to get the ' diff_dist' from the prior distribution by modifying R and Stan code
If you are only interested in rejecting the null value I think 95% HDI is enough.

Best wishes, 
Minchul

messages.subject: Re: Effect sizes
parts:
Hi Melisa,

For this, I think these two papers by John Kruschke would be helpful:

"Rejecting or Accepting Parameter Values in Bayesian Estimation"
https://journals.sagepub.com/doi/pdf/10.1177/2515245918771304

"Bayesian Assessment of Null Values Via Parameter Estimation and Model Comparison"
https://journals.sagepub.com/doi/pdf/10.1177/1745691611406925?casa_token=Q6OQ8tZ8izgAAAAA:mAPzZeEBsC_r8c062muzJHHDfqvXAu4XEI-8_8-t9ubnpqUWypId02HztXlDL5ltvJSurH2PnxpE

Best,
Young
